items.title: tranche A: bank 40-60% at +15/+20/+25 bp, rest runs (4 arms)
items.evidence: Replay fixed (tranche B breakeven). Optimistic fill model. Live gaps: rr clamp, market sell, 1R runner trail. S3/S4 (docs/TRADE_SIM.md, 776 trades 10/08-11/05, real post-fill SIP prints, price-only, trend hold OFF): tranche A: t15_60 +2.31 bp (t 6.05), t20_60 +1.38 (t 4.95), t25_60 +1.01 (t 3.57), positive in both halves, drop-5 and bootstrap p5 positive - but ALL three turn NEGATIVE with the exit delayed 1 s (-0.59/-0.31/-0.09), so the gain depends on selling at the exact target print. Live market sale latency median 0.67 s. S4 FAIL. t20_40 not shown positive. 11/07 code review: under a realistic 0.5 s exit latency in both arms the simulated gains vanish (lock50 +0.02, t15_60 -0.07, lim15 th4 -0.35 bp). S3/S4 after code review (docs/TRADE_SIM.md, 776 trades, exit latency 0.5 s both arms, 0.25 s ticks, live tranche path): tranche A NO in every form: market t15/t20/t25/t20_40 -0.50/-0.16/-0.02/-0.11 bp; resting-limit grid -0.27 to +0.19 bp, none significant. The earlier +1 to +2.6 bp gains came from stops filling at the triggering print (zero latency); they vanish under any realistic latency. 11/07 14:50: replay NOT run: the corrected trade simulator found no tranche-A gain at realistic latency and the replay's fill model is more optimistic. Parked; reopen only with a live-path fill model.

items.title: %R fast length 10 and half smoothing (rte_len, 2 arms)
items.evidence: Finished 05:20 but VACUOUS: len10 and half_both are identical to baseline (5 screen days, 133 -> 133 trades, net +0.3 -> +0.3, day delta +0). A different %R length cannot change nothing. The knob is read by live code (ai_entry_watch _rte_fast_length), so the replay probably serves %R from recorded dashboard/engine state instead of recomputing from bars (unproven). CAUSE FOUND (Argon, verified in code): ensure_live_exhaustion calls refresh_engine_exh first (ai_entry_watch.py:12465); when the recorded engine reading is Finnhub-realtime and <=8 s old (_engine_exh_fresh, :9421) it copies the engine %R (computed with 21/7/112 in signal_engine) and never reaches the local path that reads rte_fast_length. The cap `float(cfg.get(...) or 8.0)` plus max(0.5, cap) also means 0 cannot switch it off. So a replay cannot vary the %R length at all - the readings are recorded.
items.next: Do not retry in the replay. Test %R length 10 vs 21 on the SIP warehouse (compute both from bars, P2 controls) as a prereg study.
items.blocked_on: vacuous sweep: need a replay path that recomputes %R from bars, or a historical %R study on the warehouse

items.title: live %R smoothing has no EWM history: filled_clock_rows returns exactly `length` bars, so _live_percent_r_line builds a 1-element series and the EWM(7) loop never runs
items.evidence: VERIFIED in code (ai_entry_watch.py:11823-11850 with stream_bars.filled_clock_rows returning exactly length bars): live smoothed %R = one blend of the live raw value with the raw %R of the last closed window, not the 7-bar EWM the chart and signals.py use. Not in running_list or the docs I searched. Consequence unmeasured: rising/falling flags (exh_falling) may be noisier than the chart line. 11/07 narrowing (Argon, verified): this local path only runs when the engine reading is not fresh (non-realtime or >8 s old) and in trail_yields_to_triangle. The ledger does not record which path produced each poll (pctr_px_src absent), so the fraction affected is unknown.
items.next: Add pctr_px_src to the decision ledger (small, safe logging change) to measure the fraction of polls on the local path; fix only if that fraction is material.

items.title: 112-minute morning lockout: slow %R set to None before 112 bars exist, so presquare returns wait_exh until ~11:21
items.evidence: [REFUTED by measurement, not a study] REFUTED as a blanket lockout. 268,663 RTH decision-ledger polls 10/15-11/06: wait_exh (what a missing slow %R produces) is the LOWEST early: share of polls by half-hour from 09:30 = 1.5%, 4.3%, 3.0%, 4.4%, then 10.0%, 9.7%, 13.0%, 9.1%, 12.3%, 11.9%, 12.7%, 12.9%, 12.9%. items.title: code-review gate: before a tool's first result counts, the skeptic reads the tool against the live code path and a planted-edge canary must be recovered
items.evidence: Added after Argon's audit found 5 fidelity bugs in tools/trade_sim.py and a confound in the peak-lock bypass, all in code written and reported the same day. First subject: tools/trade_sim.py. FIRST REVIEW 11/07 (trade_sim.py): NOT YET. Blocking: (1) every positive delta depends on stops filling at the triggering print - with stops delayed 0.5 s in both arms lock50 +0.51 -> +0.02, t15_60 +2.55 -> -0.07, lim15_60_th4 +1.12 -> -0.35 bp; (2) S4 was rewritten after results (bc217e1d: delay only the new step) - a post-hoc pass-bar change; (3) the t*/lim* variants are not settable live (rr clamp max(0.25)) and live T1 is normally a RESTING limit attached at the first 3 s book tick, not a market sale. Major: live re-feeds the last print every 0.25 s (<=15 s old) and uses shelf ring 8; pending tranche sale lost when a stop hits first (25 trades); sim baseline != live (trend hold, dead_trade 52, no_progress 57, double_check 11, left_overbought 7, EOD 7, broker-mark low). Plumbing canary passed exactly (+4.45 vs +4.45 bp on 776 trades). REWORK 11/07 per all findings; canaries added (planted target, null knob, latency). First rerun: no variant improves. Second skeptic review still owed before any positive from this tool is used (none exists).
items.next: Apply every finding, restore the original S4 (all exits 1 s late, both arms), add the three canaries, rerun; then a second review.

items.title: position size rose ~10x on 11/05 (median ~$350 -> ~$3,280 per trade)
items.evidence: Broker round trips 10/26-11/06 (276): median position $315-$375 per trade through 11/04, $3,280/$3,269 on 11/05/11/06 (new Alpaca account created 11/04, $10K, 3 x 33%). Dollar P&L before and after is not comparable; the earlier claim that the worst 13 trades were 68% of losing dollars is mostly this size jump (11 of those 13 are 11/05-11/06). Size-neutral (bp): the worst 27 trades (10%) are 55% of losing bp, avg -58 bp, ALL 27 never-green (peak < +5 bp) vs 22% of the rest, held 556 s vs 182 s median, 21 local_trail + 6 dead_trade exits, 13 slipped past -60 bp (4.7% of all trades). Capping every loss at -60 bp would be worth only +0.28 bp/trade; at -40 bp +1.8 bp (but cuts recoveries; 60% of early cuts end better if held). OPERATOR CONFIRMED 11/07: the ~$3,300 per trade (3 x 33% of $10K) on the new account is intended. Compare weeks in bp per trip; dollars scale with size. FOLLOW-UP 11/07: the two never-green-bleed ideas (underwater leash, resting scratch) were run in the corrected simulator: none improves (X16, X17).

items.title: underwater leash (ai_local_trail_decay_red_step_r 0.005 / 0.01 / 0.02) for the never-green bleed
items.evidence: Trade simulator (776 trades, 0.5 s exit latency, corrected model): -0.60 / -0.50 / -1.00 bp per trade vs baseline, day-t -0.7 / -0.5 / -0.9, the 0.01 and 0.005 steps help the second half (+0.2 to +0.65) and hurt the first (-1.4 to -1.7). Not an improvement. Run as a simulator variant without a separate prereg (exploratory); the cells are in docs/TRADE_SIM_red_scratch.md.

items.title: resting scratch at entry after 120 / 300 / 540 s of never-green (-60 bp shelf kept as backstop)
items.evidence: Trade simulator (776 trades, 0.5 s latency; the scratch fills when a print reaches entry +2 bp, no spread paid): -1.33 / -0.16 / -0.11 bp per trade, day-t -2.7 / -0.7 / -0.8. The 2-minute scratch is clearly harmful (265 trades changed, both halves negative); 5 and 9 minutes are flat to slightly negative on 133 and 71 trades. A scratch caps the recoverers at zero and the churners it saves are too few to pay for it. Exploratory (no prereg).
